title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Free Range Eggs) Bill 2018
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Free Range Eggs) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict when eggs could be marketed as free range by imposing outdoor access, actual ranging and stocking density requirements through consumer law.
Qualifying eggs would come from hens able to range freely in daylight on most days, with a majority actually doing so and density no higher than 1,500 hens per hectare.
The bill would begin after a 12-month period following Royal Assent, and its restrictions would apply to information standards already operating or made later.
changes: Stocking density would have to appear prominently on egg labels using a hens per hectare format.
Cage-free eggs failing the free range conditions could be marketed as access to range.
Egg information standards would have no effect to the extent they permitted non-qualifying eggs to be marketed as free range.
summary.affected: Egg producers and sellers marketing eggs as free range or access to range would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The Competition and Consumer Amendment (Free Range Eggs) Bill 2018 proposes to limit 'free range' labelling to eggs from hens stocked at no more than 1,500 birds per hectare that actually roam outdoors during daylight, and to require stocking density displayed as 'hens per hectare' on cartons. The current standard allows up to 10,000 hens per hectare, which the speaker argues misleads consumers and contrasts with international standards like the EU's 2,500 birds per hectare.
